items.title: Section: Calming and Insight Are Not Divided by Object, but by Mode of Engagement

items.zh: 云何有分別影像？謂如有一，或聽聞正法、或教授教誡為所依止，或見、或聞、或分別故，於所知事同分影像、由三摩呬多地毘鉢舍那行觀察簡擇、極簡擇、遍尋思、遍伺察。所知事者，謂或不淨、或慈愍，或緣性緣起，或界差別，或阿那波那念，或蘊善巧，或界善巧，或處善巧，或緣起善巧，或處非處善巧，或下地麁性、上地靜性，或苦諦、集諦、滅諦、道諦。
items.en: What is the image accompanied by discrimination? It is like one who, relying either on the true teaching as heard or on instruction and guidance received, and through seeing, hearing, or reflecting, takes up an image corresponding to a known matter, and, within meditative equipoise, examines it through insight practice — discerning, thoroughly discerning, broadly investigating, and broadly scrutinising it. As for the known matter itself: it may be impurity, loving-kindness, dependent origination, analysis of the elements, mindfulness of breathing, skillfulness in the aggregates, in the sense-fields, in the elements, in dependent origination, in the possible and impossible, the coarseness of a lower level against the calm of a higher one, or the truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

items.title: How a Meditative Image Actually Arises: Seven Engagements and Nine Names

items.zh: 此所知事，或依教授教誡、或聽聞正法為所依止，令三摩呬多地作意現前，即於彼法而起勝解，即於彼所知事而起勝解。彼於爾時，於所知事，如現領受勝解而轉。雖彼所知事，非現領受和合現前，亦非所餘彼種類物。然由三摩呬多地勝解，領受相似作意、領受彼所知事相似顯現。由此道理，名所知事同分影像。修觀行者，推求此故，於彼本性所知事中，觀察審定功德過失。是名有分別影像。
items.en: This known matter, relying either on instruction and guidance received or on the true teaching as heard, causes meditative attention to become present, and a resolute understanding arises regarding that teaching, that known matter. At that time, one engages the known matter as though directly experiencing it in the present. … For this reason, it is called the image corresponding to the known matter. … This very image is also called the image; also called the mark of concentration; also called the field concentration operates within; also called the mouth of concentration; also called the gate of concentration; also called the locus of mental engagement; also called the mind's own internally discriminated substance; also called luminous reflection.

items.title: Section: The Image Without Discrimination — Calming's Nine Stages Revisited

items.zh: 云何無分別影像？謂修觀行者，受取如是影像相已，不復觀察簡擇、極簡擇、遍尋思、遍伺察。然即於此所緣影像，以奢摩他行寂靜其心，即是九種行相令心安住。謂令心內住、等住、安住、近住、調伏、寂靜、最極寂靜、一趣、等持。彼於爾時，成無分別影像所緣。即於如是所緣影像，一向一趣安住其念，不復觀察簡擇、極簡擇、遍尋思、遍伺察。是名無分別影像。
items.en: What is the image free of discrimination? It means that, having taken up such an image, the practitioner of meditative practice no longer discerns, thoroughly discerns, broadly investigates, or broadly scrutinises it. Rather, with regard to this very object-image, one stills the mind through calming practice, by nine modes of settling the mind: causing the mind to abide inwardly, to abide evenly, to abide steadily, to abide closely, to be tamed, to be calmed, to be utterly calmed, to become one-pointed, and to be held in balance. At that time, one accomplishes the image free of discrimination as one's object; within this very object-image, mindfulness abides single-pointedly and exclusively, no longer discerning, thoroughly discerning, broadly investigating, or broadly scrutinising it. This is called the image free of discrimination.

items.zh: 即此影像，亦名影像。亦名三摩地相，亦名三摩地所行境界，亦名三摩地口，亦名三摩地門，亦名作意處，亦名內分別體，亦名光影。如是等類，當知名為所知事同分影像諸名差別。

items.title: Section: The Limit of Things — Exhaustive Particulars and Universal Nature Together

items.zh: 云何事邊際性？謂若所緣盡所有性、如所有性。云何名為盡所有性？謂色蘊外更無餘色，受想行識蘊外更無有餘受想行識；一切有為事，皆五法所攝；一切諸法，界處所攝；一切所知事，四聖諦攝。
items.en: What is the limit of things? It is the object taken as both its exhaustive particulars and its universal nature. What is meant by exhaustive particulars? It means that beyond the aggregate of form there is no further form, and beyond the aggregates of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness there is no further feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness; every conditioned matter is comprised within these five; all phenomena are comprised within the elements and sense-fields; and every known matter is comprised within the Four Noble Truths.

items.title: Section: Universal Nature Closes the Limit of Things

items.zh: 云何名為如所有性？謂若所緣是真實性、是真如性，由四道理，具道理性。謂觀待道理、作用道理、證成道理、法爾道理。如是若所緣境盡所有性、如所有性，總說為一事邊際性。
items.en: What is meant by universal nature? It means that the object is taken as its true, unchanging nature — its suchness — established through four principles: the principle of dependence, the principle of function, the principle of proof, and the principle of natural law. In this way, an object's exhaustive particulars and its universal nature, taken together, are called, as one, the limit of things.

items.title: Section: Task Accomplished — The Fourth Pervasive Object, and the Category Closes

items.zh: 云何所作成辦？謂修觀行者，於奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，若修、若習、若多修習為因緣故，諸緣影像所有作意皆得圓滿。此圓滿故，便得轉依，一切麁重悉皆息滅。得轉依故，超過影像，即於所知事，有無分別現量智見生。入初靜慮者，得初靜慮時，於初靜慮所行境界；入第二第三第四靜慮者，得第二第三第四靜慮時，於第二第三第四靜慮所行境界；入空無邊處、識無邊處、無所有處、非想非非想處者，得彼定時，即於彼定所行境界。
items.en: What is task accomplished? It means that, through cultivating, repeating, and extensively practising calming and insight, all the mental engagements connected with these object-images reach completion. Because of this completion, one attains a transformation of one's basis, and every coarse residue is entirely extinguished. Because of this transformation, one goes beyond mere images, and non-discriminating knowledge and vision of direct perception arises with respect to the known matter itself. For one who enters the first absorption, this occurs within the first absorption's own domain upon attaining it; for one who enters the second, third, or fourth, within each of their own domains; and for one who enters the spheres of infinite space, infinite consciousness, nothingness, or neither-perception-nor-non-perception, within each of those domains upon attaining them.

blocks.text: What exactly does one meditate on? Not the object itself, the treatise says, but an **image** (影像) of it in the mind. This is a key Yogācāra idea, and is central to the *Saṃdhinirmocana Sūtra*'s chapter on meditation.

Relying on the teaching heard or on instruction, the practitioner "takes up an image corresponding to a known matter, and within meditative equipoise examines it through insight". The thing itself is not present; what is present is "an image resembling it". Venerable Miào Jìng: "hearing the teaching" applies to sharp faculties; "instruction" to those who follow others.
The image is also called the mark of concentration, its domain, its mouth, its gate, the locus of attention, the internal substance, the reflected appearance.

Having taken up the image, the practitioner "no longer discerns, investigates, or scrutinises it", but settles the mind through the **nine stages of mental abiding**: abiding inwardly, evenly, steadily, closely; tamed; calmed; thoroughly calmed; one-pointed; in equipoise. Master Cháng Bǎi: "free of discrimination" does not mean without an image; calm stills the discrimination, not the image.

Taken as both its **exhaustive particulars** (盡所有性: "beyond the five aggregates there is no further phenomenon") and its **universal nature** (如所有性: suchness, established by the four principles of Day 212). Master Cháng Bǎi: one must still see each dependent phenomenon clearly, to see their nature.

Through calm and insight practised repeatedly, the work completes, and "one attains a transformation of one's basis, and every coarse residue is entirely extinguished". This is the **transformation of the basis** (轉依), the goal of Yogācāra practice.

quiz.q: What image does Venerable Miào Jìng use for "corresponding" in "the image corresponding to the known matter"?
options: the noodles you picture in your mind are like the noodles your eyes saw
quiz.why: "Takes up an image corresponding to a known matter, and, within meditative equipoise, examines it through insight practice." Venerable Miào Jìng: the noodles you think of are like the noodles your eyes saw — that is "corresponding."

quiz.q: What other names does the corresponding image have, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "the mouth of concentration"?
options: also image, mark of concentration, its field, mouth, gate, locus of attention, internal discriminated substance, luminous reflection; with this object in mind, concentration gradually emerges
quiz.why: "This very image is also called the image; the mark of concentration … the mouth of concentration; the gate of concentration; the locus of mental engagement; the mind's own internally discriminated substance; luminous reflection." Venerable Miào Jìng: because you hold this object in mind, concentration gradually comes forth.

quiz.q: By which nine modes does the image free of discrimination settle the mind, and to what concentration does Venerable Miào Jìng assign this process?
options: abiding inwardly, evenly, steadily, closely, tamed, calmed, utterly calmed, one-pointed, balanced; the process from first sitting to desire-realm concentration
quiz.why: "Causing the mind to abide inwardly, to abide evenly, to abide steadily, to abide closely, to be tamed, to be calmed, to be utterly calmed, to become one-pointed, and to be held in balance." Venerable Miào Jìng: stilling the mind here is within desire-realm concentration — from first sitting until that concentration succeeds, the process has nine aspects.

quiz.q: Does the "image free of discrimination" mean having no object? What do the masters say?
options: both agree: not markless — the image remains, only no discrimination is made on it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "free of discrimination" does not mean markless — the object-image is still there; calming stills the mind so it no longer searches or discriminates the image. Venerable Miào Jìng: no false discrimination on the object is what "image free of discrimination" means; there is still an object.

quiz.q: What are "exhaustive particulars," and how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "the limit of things"?
options: beyond the aggregates nothing more; all conditioned things in the five, all phenomena in elements and fields, all knowables in the four truths; every dependently arisen thing within the limit of the knowable is taken in
quiz.why: "Beyond the aggregate of form there is no further form … every conditioned matter is comprised within these five; all phenomena within the elements and sense-fields; every known matter within the Four Noble Truths." Master Cháng Bǎi: beyond this it is no longer the matter; every dependently arisen thing within the bounds of the knowable is taken in — that is the limit of things.

quiz.q: How do the masters relate "suchness" to dependent origination?
options: Cháng Bǎi: suchness is not apart from dependent origination, so exhaustive particulars must still be cultivated; Miào Jìng: suchness is non-difference, while dependent things appear differentiated
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: why must one still cultivate exhaustive particulars and see each dependent phenomenon clearly? Because suchness is not apart from dependent origination. Venerable Miào Jìng: suchness means non-difference; dependently arisen things show differing appearances.

quiz.q: In task-accomplished, transformation of the basis extinguishes all coarse residue. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say "coarse residue" is?
options: the seeds of affliction — all of them
quiz.why: "Because of this completion, one attains a transformation of one's basis, and every coarse residue is entirely extinguished." Venerable Miào Jìng: coarse residue, truly speaking, is the seeds of affliction — all of them.
